Water damage grows by the hour. The first five minutes on the phone decide how bad the day gets.
On the phone
Ask first if anyone is hurt or if water is near electrical outlets.
Walk the caller to the main shutoff and have them close it.
Take the address, a callback number and two photos if they can send them.
Dispatch
Pick the nearest plumber with a loaded van.
Text the customer the plumber name and a 30 minute window.
Mark the job Emergency priority and Scheduled for today.
After the visit
If the damage is large, tell the customer to call their insurer and give them a written list of what was found. Do not guess at coverage.
A standard swap takes four to five hours. Plan the truck and the permit before the day.
The day before
Confirm the heater size and fuel type.
Check the permit is filed with the city.
Load the heater, expansion tank, new supply lines and venting.
On site
Shut off water and gas or power and drain the old tank.
Set the new unit, connect, test for leaks and light it.
Set the temperature with the customer and show the shutoffs.
Wrap up
Haul the old tank, photograph the installed unit and its label, and enter parts and hours before you leave.
Plumbers lose more time to a missing fitting than to any hard repair. Restock every Friday.
Steps
Count each van against its par list.
Update On hand on the Parts list.
Put every Reorder row on the supplier call.
Load fresh stock before the weekend on-call plumber leaves.
